entries.meaning: In a morally right way, or with a justified feeling that something is wrong. ---
examples: She was righteously angry about how the workers had been treated.
He tried to live righteously and help his neighbors.
Parents righteously demanded answers from the school board.
entries.position: end — also before an adjective (righteously indignant)

entries.meaning: According to what is fair, legal or deserved. ---
examples: The money rightfully belongs to her children.
She is rightfully proud of what she built.
After the war, the painting was returned to the family it rightfully belonged to.
entries.position: mid — before the main verb or participle; also end
entries.contrast: Rightfully is about what someone has a right to (the land rightfully belongs to them = по праву). Rightly is about being correct (She rightly guessed = верно угадала). In rightly proud either word can appear.

entries.meaning: In a stiff or strict way that does not bend or change. ---
examples: The dress code is rigidly enforced.
He sat rigidly in his chair, afraid to move.
The schedule is followed rigidly, down to the minute.
entries.position: end — also before a participle (rigidly enforced)

entries.meaning: Very carefully and thoroughly, following strict standards. ---
examples: Every new drug is rigorously tested before approval.
The rules are applied rigorously.
She trained rigorously for the Boston Marathon.
entries.position: end — also before a participle (rigorously tested)

entries.meaning: In a wild, uncontrolled way, or to a wildly high degree. ---
examples: The show is riotously funny from start to finish.
The garden was riotously colorful in June.
Fans celebrated riotously in the streets after the win.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (riotously funny); also end

entries.meaning: As part of a ritual, or always in the same fixed way. ---
examples: The animals were ritually sacrificed to the gods.
Every Friday, the office ritually orders pizza.
Politicians ritually promise to cut taxes.

entries.meaning: Extremely, noisily, in roaring drunk. ---
examples: By midnight the best man was roaring drunk.
He came home roaring drunk and woke the whole building.
They got roaring drunk after the championship game.
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective roaring
entries.contrast: Elsewhere roaring is an adjective: a roaring fire (жарко пылающий), a roaring success (оглушительный успех), the Roaring Twenties.

entries.meaning: In a strong, healthy or vigorous way. ---
examples: The economy grew robustly in the second quarter.
The cabinet is robustly built from solid oak.
She defended her position robustly at the hearing.
entries.position: end — also before a participle (robustly built)

entries.meaning: Romantically has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The two actors were romantically involved for years.
Are you seeing anyone romantically right now?
He's not interested in her romantically.
The table was set romantically with candles and roses.
She talks romantically about life on a farm, but she's never lived on one.

senses.head: In a way that is connected with love relationships
examples: The two actors were romantically involved for years.
Are you seeing anyone romantically right now?
He's not interested in her romantically.

senses.head: In a way that is full of love, beauty or idealized feeling
examples: The table was set romantically with candles and roses.
She talks romantically about life on a farm, but she's never lived on one.

entries.position: end — in the manner sense; before its word in romantically involved

entries.meaning: In a violent or careless way, not gently. ---
examples: The older kids played rough, and someone always ended up crying.
Hockey teams tend to play rougher in the playoffs.
Those movers treated our furniture pretty rough.
entries.modifies: a few verbs: play, treat, handle
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective rough
entries.contrast: Informal and limited to set phrases like play rough. In most sentences the adverb is roughly: He grabbed her arm roughly. Roughly also means approximately, which rough never does. British sleep rough (ночевать на улице) is rare in American English.

entries.meaning: Roughly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The drive takes roughly three hours.
Roughly half the students take the bus.
Roughly speaking, the two plans cost the same.
The officer grabbed him roughly by the arm.
Don't handle the package so roughly — it's glass.

senses.head: Approximately; not exactly
examples: The drive takes roughly three hours.
Roughly half the students take the bus.
Roughly speaking, the two plans cost the same.

senses.head: In a violent or careless way, not gently
examples: The officer grabbed him roughly by the arm.
Don't handle the package so roughly — it's glass.

entries.position: before its word — before a number or amount; end in the not gently sense
entries.comparison: not gradable — in the approximately sense; more/most for not gently

entries.meaning: Strongly, thoroughly and by many people. ---
examples: The plan was roundly criticized by both parties.
The champions were roundly beaten in the first round.
Critics roundly condemned the decision.
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (roundly criticized); also end
entries.modifies: verbs and participles of criticism and defeat

entries.meaning: Royally has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The guests were treated royally at the wedding.
Our hosts fed us royally all weekend.
The team was royally welcomed back home after the title.
I royally messed up that presentation.
We got royally ripped off by that contractor.

senses.head: In a grand or generous way, as if for a king or queen
examples: The guests were treated royally at the wedding.
Our hosts fed us royally all weekend.
The team was royally welcomed back home after the title.

senses.head: Completely and badly, in informal speech
examples: I royally messed up that presentation.
We got royally ripped off by that contractor.

entries.position: end — after the verb or its object
entries.comparison: not gradable — though more royally occurs in the like royalty sense

entries.meaning: In an impolite way, or suddenly and unpleasantly. ---
examples: The waiter spoke to us very rudely.
He rudely interrupted her in the middle of a sentence.
I was rudely awakened by a garbage truck at 5 a.m.

entries.meaning: In a way that shows you are sorry or a little sad about something, often with a wry smile. ---
examples: "I should have listened to you," he admitted ruefully.
She smiled ruefully at the burned cookies.
He shook his head ruefully when he saw the bill.

entries.meaning: In a strong, tough or rough-looking way. ---
examples: The actor was ruggedly handsome, with a scar on his chin.
The phone is ruggedly built to survive a fall.
The coast there is ruggedly beautiful.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective or participle (ruggedly handsome)

entries.meaning: To a degree that causes financial ruin or serious damage. ---
examples: Health care in the U.S. can be ruinously expensive.
The lawsuit turned out to be ruinously costly for the company.
Interest rates on those loans are ruinously high.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (ruinously expensive)

entries.meaning: Without pity or concern for others. ---
examples: The dictator ruthlessly crushed all opposition.
She edited the essay ruthlessly, cutting half of it.
The company is ruthlessly efficient about cutting costs.
entries.position: end — also mid, and before an adjective (ruthlessly efficient)

entries.meaning: Safely has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The plane landed safely despite the storm.
Please drive safely — the roads are icy.
Store your passwords more safely than on a sticky note.
I think we can safely say the project was a success.
You can safely ignore that warning message.

senses.head: Without harm, danger or damage
examples: The plane landed safely despite the storm.
Please drive safely — the roads are icy.
Store your passwords more safely than on a sticky note.

senses.head: With little risk of being wrong, in can safely say and can safely assume
examples: I think we can safely say the project was a success.
You can safely ignore that warning message.

entries.position: end — in the without harm sense; mid after a modal in can safely say

entries.meaning: In a wise way, or in a way meant to look wise. ---
examples: Grandpa nodded sagely and said nothing.
"Money doesn't buy happiness," she said sagely.
The experts sagely predicted what everyone already knew.

entries.meaning: In a way that shows you think you are morally better than other people. ---
examples: He sanctimoniously reminded everyone that he never drinks.
"Some of us actually read the instructions," she said sanctimoniously.
The ad lectures viewers sanctimoniously about healthy eating.

entries.meaning: In a mocking way that says the opposite of what is meant. ---
examples: "Oh, great, another meeting," he said sarcastically.
She sarcastically thanked him for being on time for once.
Don't answer your teacher sarcastically.

entries.meaning: In a scornful, grimly mocking way. ---
examples: He smiled sardonically when they asked if he was enjoying the party.
"What a surprise," she remarked sardonically.
The comedian sardonically described his own failed marriage.

entries.meaning: In a way that uses humor to criticize people or ideas. ---
examples: The show portrays Washington politicians satirically.
The article was written satirically, but many readers took it seriously.
The cartoon satirically shows the CEO as a pig.

entries.meaning: Well enough to meet a need or standard. ---
examples: The problem was resolved satisfactorily.
Students must complete the course satisfactorily to graduate.
Nobody could explain satisfactorily why the money was missing.
entries.position: end — after the verb or its object
entries.form: -ly from satisfactory, with y changing to i

entries.meaning: In a way that gives pleasure or a sense of completion. ---
examples: The fries were satisfyingly crunchy.
The mystery ends satisfyingly, with every clue explained.
The door closed with a satisfyingly solid thud.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (satisfyingly crunchy); also end

entries.meaning: In a very violent or cruel way, including in harsh criticism. ---
examples: The hiker was savagely attacked by a bear.
Critics savagely panned the new movie.
The two dogs fought savagely over the bone.
entries.position: end — also mid, and before a participle (savagely beaten)

entries.meaning: In a shocking way, or to a shocking and unacceptable degree. ---
examples: Teachers in this state are scandalously underpaid.
The prices at the stadium are scandalously high.
The landlord behaved scandalously toward his tenants.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective or participle (scandalously low); also end

entries.meaning: In a way that gives too little, especially too little clothing. ---
examples: The ad showed scantily clad models on a beach.
The room was scantily furnished with a bed and one chair.
The dancers were scantily dressed for such a cold night.
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (scantily clad)
entries.form: -ly from scanty, with y changing to i

entries.meaning: In a frightening way, or to a surprisingly high degree. ---
examples: The app's predictions are scarily accurate.
The car came scarily close to hitting the kids.
She's scarily good at poker.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (scarily accurate)
entries.form: -ly from scary, with y changing to i

entries.meaning: In a very harsh, critical way. ---
examples: The report scathingly criticized the police response.
She wrote scathingly about the restaurant's service.
He spoke scathingly of his former boss.

entries.meaning: Extremely, in scorching hot. ---
examples: It was scorching hot in Phoenix all week.
Be careful — the pan handle is scorching hot.
The sand was scorching hot, so we ran to the water.
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective scorching
entries.contrast: Usually scorching is an adjective: a scorching day, a scorching review (разгромная рецензия). As an adverb it only intensifies hot.

entries.meaning: In a way that shows you think someone or something is worthless. ---
examples: She laughed scornfully at his offer.
"You call that a car?" he said scornfully.
The critics looked scornfully on reality TV.

entries.meaning: Without being punished or paying for what you did. ---
examples: The real criminals got off scot-free.
He crashed my car and walked away scot-free.
It isn't fair that she went scot-free.
entries.position: end — almost always after get off, go or walk away

entries.meaning: Very carefully and completely, paying attention to every detail. ---
examples: The kitchen was kept scrupulously clean.
She is scrupulously honest about her expenses.
The researchers followed the protocol scrupulously.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (scrupulously clean); also end

entries.meaning: In a way that tries hard to find out what someone thinks or feels. ---
examples: She looked at him searchingly, waiting for the truth.
The detective stared searchingly into the suspect's eyes.
"Are you really okay?" he asked searchingly.

entries.meaning: In a way that is normal for the time of year, especially of weather. ---
examples: Expect seasonably cool temperatures through the weekend.
It's been seasonably warm for late May.
The forecast calls for seasonably dry weather in the valley.
entries.type: degree — as usual for the season
entries.position: before its word — before a weather adjective (seasonably warm)
entries.contrast: Seasonably warm means as warm as is normal for the time of year (по сезону). Seasonally means 'according to the season' (seasonally adjusted figures, seasonally available fruit). The opposite is unseasonably (не по сезону).

entries.meaning: According to the season, or changing with the seasons. ---
examples: The unemployment figures are seasonally adjusted.
The menu changes seasonally.
Many workers here are employed seasonally on farms.
entries.position: end — also before a participle (seasonally adjusted)

entries.meaning: Toward the sea, away from land. ---
examples: The boats drifted seaward with the tide.
The house faces seaward, with a view of the bay.
The storm moved seaward overnight.
entries.position: end — after a verb of movement or facing
entries.form: -ward — direction; British English also uses seawards

entries.meaning: Second has 2 distinct senses.
examples: First, it's too expensive. Second, nobody asked for it.
