I didn't go because, first, I was sick, and second, I had no ride.
She finished second in the 400 meters.
Our team came in second again this year.

senses.head: As the second point in a list of reasons or steps
examples: First, it's too expensive. Second, nobody asked for it.
Second, make sure the power is off before you start.
I didn't go because, first, I was sick, and second, I had no ride.

senses.head: In second place in a race, contest or order
examples: She finished second in the 400 meters.
Our team came in second again this year.

entries.position: front or end — front for listing points; end after finish, come in, rank
entries.modifies: the whole sentence; verbs of ranking
entries.form: flat — the same form as the ordinal second
entries.contrast: When listing points, Americans usually say First, … Second, … Third, …; secondly is also correct, a little more formal. In the second largest city the word is an ordinal, and many writers hyphenate it: second-largest.

entries.meaning: As a less important or later part; not mainly. ---
examples: The app is mainly for messaging and only secondarily for photos.
The infection spread secondarily to the lungs.
She sees herself as a teacher first and secondarily as a researcher.
entries.position: mid or end — often after only
entries.form: -ly from secondary, with y changing to i

entries.meaning: Secondhand has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We bought most of our furniture secondhand.
I got this bike secondhand for fifty bucks.
Textbooks are much cheaper if you buy them secondhand.
I only heard about the fight secondhand, so I can't say who started it.
The news reached us secondhand, through a neighbor.

senses.head: After someone else has already owned or used it
examples: We bought most of our furniture secondhand.
I got this bike secondhand for fifty bucks.
Textbooks are much cheaper if you buy them secondhand.

senses.head: From another person, not directly from the source
examples: I only heard about the fight secondhand, so I can't say who started it.
The news reached us secondhand, through a neighbor.

entries.русский: подержанным, с рук; из вторых рук
entries.form: compound — second + hand; also spelled second-hand

entries.meaning: As the second point in a list of reasons or steps. ---
examples: Firstly, the plan is too expensive; secondly, it takes too long.
Secondly, all applicants must pass a background check.
I'm not going because, firstly, it's raining and, secondly, I'm tired.
entries.contrast: American English more often lists with First, … Second, …. Firstly, secondly sound a bit more formal or British, but both patterns are correct. Do not mix them in one list.

entries.meaning: In a way that hides information or feelings from others. ---
examples: The kids whispered secretively in the corner.
He smiled secretively and wouldn't tell us where he'd been.
The company has acted very secretively about its new phone.
entries.contrast: Secretively describes behavior that hides things or looks mysterious (скрытно). Secretly says the action itself was kept secret (тайно): They met secretly = тайно встречались; He smiled secretively = загадочно улыбнулся.

entries.meaning: Secretly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The couple secretly got married in Las Vegas.
He had been secretly recording their phone calls.
The documents were moved secretly at night.
I secretly hoped the game would be canceled.
Everyone was secretly relieved when he left.

senses.head: Without other people knowing or seeing
examples: The couple secretly got married in Las Vegas.
He had been secretly recording their phone calls.
The documents were moved secretly at night.

senses.head: Privately, in your own mind, without telling anyone
examples: I secretly hoped the game would be canceled.
Everyone was secretly relieved when he left.

entries.position: mid — before the main verb; also end

entries.meaning: Firmly or safely, so that it cannot move, open or be reached by others. ---
examples: Make sure your seatbelt is securely fastened.
All customer data is stored securely.
Lock the gate securely before you leave.
entries.position: end — after the verb or its object; also before a participle (securely fastened)

entries.meaning: In a calm, slow and dignified way. ---
examples: The old couple walked sedately along the boardwalk.
The paddleboat moved sedately down the river.
He drove sedately, well under the speed limit.

entries.meaning: In an attractive way that tempts or draws people in. ---
examples: She smiled seductively across the table.
The idea is seductively simple, but it doesn't work.
The ad seductively promises you'll lose weight without trying.
entries.position: end — also before an adjective (seductively simple)

entries.meaning: By choosing only some things or people, not all. ---
examples: He quotes the report selectively to support his argument.
The museum collects selectively, focusing on local artists.
Kids tend to listen selectively when you ask them to clean up.

entries.meaning: In a nervous or embarrassed way, aware that others are watching. ---
examples: She tugged self-consciously at her dress.
He laughed self-consciously when everyone turned to look at him.
The new kid stood self-consciously at the front of the class.
entries.contrast: False friend: self-conscious is not сознательный (that is conscientious or responsible). It means embarrassed and aware of being watched: He laughed self-consciously = смущённо засмеялся. It can also mean 'deliberately, with awareness' in writing about art: a self-consciously retro design.

entries.meaning: So clearly that it needs no proof or explanation. ---
examples: The claim is self-evidently false.
Self-evidently, a bridge needs to hold more than its own weight.
What seems self-evidently true to one generation is questioned by the next.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (self-evidently true); also front with a comma

entries.meaning: In a way that shows you are sure you are right and others are wrong. ---
examples: He self-righteously lectured us about recycling while holding a plastic bottle.
"I would never cheat," she said self-righteously.
The senator spoke self-righteously about family values.

entries.meaning: Thinking only of yourself and not of others. ---
examples: He selfishly ate the last slice without asking anyone.
She acted selfishly and left us to clean up.
Selfishly, I was glad the trip was canceled, because I needed the rest.

entries.meaning: Caring more about others than about yourself. ---
examples: The nurses worked selflessly through the pandemic.
She selflessly gave her seat on the lifeboat to a child.
He served his community selflessly for forty years.

entries.meaning: In terms of meaning, especially of words or sentences. ---
examples: Big and large are semantically similar but not always interchangeable.
Semantically, the two sentences say the same thing.
The sentence is grammatical but semantically odd.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (semantically similar); also front with a comma
entries.modifies: adjectives and verbs; or the whole sentence

entries.meaning: Twice a year; every six months. ---
examples: Interest on the bond is paid semiannually.
The committee meets semiannually, in March and September.
We review everyone's salary semiannually.
entries.contrast: Semiannually means twice a year, every six months (раз в полгода). Biannually also means twice a year, but biennially means every two years — easy to mix up, so business writing prefers semiannually.

entries.meaning: Twice a month. ---
examples: Employees are paid semimonthly, on the 1st and the 15th.
The newsletter comes out semimonthly.
Rent can be paid monthly or semimonthly.
entries.contrast: Semimonthly is twice a month, usually on fixed dates like the 1st and 15th (24 paychecks a year). Biweekly is every two weeks (26 paychecks). Bimonthly is ambiguous — it can mean every two months or twice a month.

entries.meaning: Sensationally has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The new album has been sensationally successful.
The food was sensationally good.
She played sensationally in the final.
The tabloids reported the murder sensationally.
Cable news covered the trial sensationally for weeks.

senses.head: Extremely well, or to an amazing degree
examples: The new album has been sensationally successful.
The food was sensationally good.
She played sensationally in the final.

senses.head: In a shocking, exaggerated way meant to attract attention
examples: The tabloids reported the murder sensationally.
Cable news covered the trial sensationally for weeks.

entries.position: before its word — before an adjective (sensationally good); end in the exaggerated sense

entries.meaning: Without any good reason or purpose. ---
examples: Three people were senselessly killed in the shooting.
The old trees were cut down senselessly.
They argued senselessly about who was to blame.
entries.position: end — also before a participle (senselessly killed)

entries.meaning: In a practical, reasonable way that shows good judgment. ---
examples: Dress sensibly — it gets cold in the mountains at night.
She sensibly saved part of every paycheck.
The kids behaved sensibly and called 911 right away.
entries.contrast: False friend: sensibly is not чувствительно — that is sensitively. Sensible means разумный: dress sensibly = одеться практично, по погоде; handle it sensitively = подойти деликатно.

entries.meaning: With care for other people's feelings or for a delicate situation. ---
examples: The teacher handled the bullying case very sensitively.
The movie deals sensitively with the subject of grief.
Doctors need to break bad news sensitively.
entries.position: end — after the verb or its object

entries.meaning: In a way that gives or expresses physical pleasure. ---
examples: The dancers moved slowly and sensually.
She described the food sensually, almost like poetry.
The singer's voice was sensually low and smoky.

entries.meaning: In a way that pleases or appeals to the senses. ---
examples: The cat stretched sensuously in the sun.
The paint is applied sensuously, in thick, rich strokes.
The cello melody rose sensuously over the orchestra.
entries.contrast: Sensuously is about pleasure to the senses — sound, color, texture, taste (the cat stretched sensuously). Sensually more often suggests physical or sexual pleasure. The two overlap, but sensuous is the safer word for art, music and food.

entries.meaning: Because of feelings and memories, rather than practical reasons. ---
examples: The ring isn't worth much, but I'm sentimentally attached to it.
He spoke sentimentally about his hometown.
The old truck is valuable only sentimentally.
entries.position: end — also before an adjective (sentimentally attached)

entries.meaning: Apart from others; not together. ---
examples: Wash the dark clothes separately.
The two suspects were questioned separately.
Batteries are sold separately.
entries.position: end — after the verb or its object

entries.meaning: One after another, in a fixed order. ---
examples: The pages are numbered sequentially.
The tasks must be completed sequentially, not all at once.
The files are processed sequentially by the server.
entries.position: end — also before a participle (sequentially numbered)

entries.meaning: In a calm, peaceful way, untroubled by what is happening. ---
examples: She smiled serenely while everyone else panicked.
The lake lay serenely under the morning fog.
The baby slept serenely through the fireworks.

entries.meaning: One after another, in a series or in installments. ---
examples: The novel was first published serially in a magazine.
All the tickets are serially numbered.
The old computer processed the tasks serially, not in parallel.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (serially numbered)

entries.meaning: By seven times as much. ---
examples: The number of users grew sevenfold in two years.
Home prices in the area have risen almost sevenfold since 1990.
The new engine increased the plane's range sevenfold.
entries.modifies: verbs such as increase, grow, rise

entries.meaning: Severely has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Two people were severely injured in the crash.
The storm severely damaged the roof.
Our budget is severely limited this year.
Cheating on the exam will be punished severely.
The judge spoke severely to the young man.
She was dressed severely in a black suit.
Her hair was pulled back severely into a bun.

senses.head: Very badly or seriously
examples: Two people were severely injured in the crash.
The storm severely damaged the roof.
Our budget is severely limited this year.

senses.head: Strictly or harshly
examples: Cheating on the exam will be punished severely.
The judge spoke severely to the young man.

senses.head: In a very plain style, with no decoration
examples: She was dressed severely in a black suit.
Her hair was pulled back severely into a bun.

entries.position: mid or end — mid before a participle (severely injured)

entries.meaning: In a way that relates to sex. ---
examples: Some infections are sexually transmitted.
The survey asked teenagers whether they were sexually active.
She reported that she had been sexually harassed at work.
entries.position: before its word — usually before an adjective or participle

entries.meaning: Shabbily has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A shabbily dressed man asked us for change.
The hotel lobby was shabbily furnished.
I think the company treated her very shabbily.
After twenty years of service, he was shabbily fired by email.

senses.head: In old, worn or poor-looking clothes or condition
examples: A shabbily dressed man asked us for change.
The hotel lobby was shabbily furnished.

senses.head: Unfairly or without respect
examples: I think the company treated her very shabbily.
After twenty years of service, he was shabbily fired by email.

entries.position: end — or before a participle (shabbily dressed)

entries.meaning: In an unsteady, trembling or uncertain way. ---
examples: He stood up shakily after the fall.
"I'm fine," she said shakily.
The team started the season shakily but finished strong.

entries.meaning: Not deeply. ---
examples: The patient was breathing shallowly.
Plant the seeds shallowly, about a quarter inch down.
The book treats a serious topic rather shallowly.

entries.meaning: In an embarrassed way that shows you feel ashamed. ---
examples: He grinned shamefacedly and admitted he had forgotten.
The kids shamefacedly returned the candy they had taken.
She looked down shamefacedly when the teacher called her name.

entries.meaning: In a way that deserves shame or disgrace. ---
examples: The veterans were treated shamefully when they came home.
Teachers in the state are shamefully underpaid.
He behaved shamefully at his brother's wedding.
entries.position: end — or before an adjective (shamefully low)

entries.meaning: Without feeling any shame or embarrassment. ---
examples: The ad shamelessly copies a famous movie scene.
He flirted shamelessly with every waitress.
I'm going to shamelessly ask you all to buy my book.

entries.meaning: In an embarrassed way, usually after a silly mistake. ---
examples: He smiled sheepishly and said he'd locked his keys in the car.
"I forgot your birthday," she admitted sheepishly.
The dog looked up sheepishly from the torn pillow.

entries.meaning: In a way that looks dishonest or suspicious, often avoiding people's eyes. ---
examples: The man glanced shiftily around the parking lot before opening the trunk.
He answered the detective's questions shiftily.
Her eyes moved shiftily from the door to the window.

entries.meaning: Shockingly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The food was shockingly expensive.
A shockingly high number of students drop out in the first year.
The movie was shockingly bad.
Shockingly, nobody was hurt in the explosion.
Shockingly, the report was never made public.

senses.head: To a surprising and upsetting degree
examples: The food was shockingly expensive.
A shockingly high number of students drop out in the first year.
The movie was shockingly bad.

senses.head: Used to say that a fact is surprising or upsetting
examples: Shockingly, nobody was hurt in the explosion.
Shockingly, the report was never made public.

entries.position: before its word — or front as a comment on the whole sentence
entries.modifies: adjectives and adverbs; a whole clause

entries.meaning: Badly and carelessly made or done. ---
examples: The houses were shoddily built and fell apart within years.
The repair was done shoddily, and the leak came back.
The case was shoddily investigated from the start.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (shoddily built)

entries.meaning: Side by side and close together; also, united in support of each other. ---
examples: Fans stood shoulder to shoulder in the packed stadium.
Volunteers worked shoulder to shoulder to fill sandbags.
The two parties stood shoulder to shoulder against the new law.
entries.modifies: verbs such as stand, work, fight
entries.contrast: Written without hyphens after a verb (stand shoulder to shoulder); hyphenated before a noun, where it is an adjective (a shoulder-to-shoulder crowd).

entries.meaning: In a clever, practical way that shows good judgment. ---
examples: She shrewdly bought the land before prices went up.
He looked at me shrewdly, as if he knew I was lying.
The company invested its profits shrewdly.

entries.meaning: In a high, loud and unpleasant voice or sound. ---
examples: The whistle blew shrilly.
"Get out of my kitchen!" she screamed shrilly.
Critics complained shrilly about the new tax.

entries.meaning: In a nervous, timid way around other people. ---
examples: The little girl smiled shyly from behind her mother.
He shyly asked her to dance.
"Thank you," she said shyly.

entries.meaning: Written exactly this way in the original, mistake included. ---
examples: The sign in the window read "Open Sundy's [sic]."
In his letter he said he was "very greatful [sic] for the help."
The memo stated that the meeting was "definately [sic] on Friday."
entries.type: stance — the writer's note that a mistake is quoted exactly
entries.position: after its word — in square brackets inside a quotation
entries.modifies: the quoted word or phrase just before it
entries.contrast: Latin for 'thus'. It says the mistake belongs to the original, not to the person quoting it. Not the verb sic (sic the dog on someone, натравить).

entries.meaning: In a way that makes you feel sick; to an unpleasant degree. ---
examples: The frosting was sickeningly sweet.
The car lurched sickeningly toward the edge of the cliff.
They're sickeningly cheerful first thing in the morning.
entries.position: before its word — or end after a verb

entries.meaning: With the arm moving to the side, level with the shoulder or lower, not over the head. ---
examples: The relief pitcher throws sidearm.
She skipped the stone sidearm across the pond.
He dropped down and threw sidearm to first base.
entries.contrast: As a noun, a sidearm is a pistol worn at the side (police officers carry sidearms).

entries.meaning: Sitting with both legs on one side of a horse, bike or other seat. ---
examples: In old photos, women often rode sidesaddle.
She sat sidesaddle on the back of his motorcycle.
The actress learned to ride sidesaddle for the film.

entries.meaning: So much that you laugh very hard. ---
examples: The show was sidesplittingly funny.
He told a sidesplittingly funny story about his first job.
Her impressions of our boss are sidesplittingly accurate.

entries.meaning: Significantly has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Prices have risen significantly since last year.
The new model is significantly faster.
Exercise can significantly reduce the risk of heart disease.
Significantly, the mayor did not attend the meeting.
More significantly, the drug had no serious side effects.
She looked significantly at her husband.
He paused significantly before answering.

senses.head: By a large or noticeable amount
examples: Prices have risen significantly since last year.
The new model is significantly faster.
Exercise can significantly reduce the risk of heart disease.

senses.head: Used to say that a fact is important or tells you something
examples: Significantly, the mayor did not attend the meeting.
More significantly, the drug had no serious side effects.

senses.head: In a way that suggests a hidden meaning
examples: She looked significantly at her husband.
He paused significantly before answering.

entries.position: mid or end — before a comparative (significantly better); front as a comment
entries.modifies: verbs, comparatives and adjectives; a whole clause

entries.meaning: Without speaking or making any sound. ---
examples: We sat silently and waited for the news.
The door slid open silently.
She silently read the letter twice.

entries.meaning: At the same time. ---
examples: The two bombs went off almost simultaneously.
The movie will be released simultaneously in theaters and online.
It's hard to listen and take notes simultaneously.

entries.meaning: Sincerely has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I sincerely hope you feel better soon.
We sincerely apologize for the delay.
He sincerely believed he was helping.
Sincerely, Maria Lopez
End the cover letter with "Sincerely yours" and your full name.

senses.head: Honestly and really meaning what you say or feel
examples: I sincerely hope you feel better soon.
We sincerely apologize for the delay.
He sincerely believed he was helping.

senses.head: Used to close a formal letter or email, before your name
examples: Sincerely, Maria Lopez
End the cover letter with "Sincerely yours" and your full name.

entries.position: mid — before the verb; end is also possible
entries.contrast: The letter closing is Sincerely or Sincerely yours in American English; British English prefers Yours sincerely.

entries.meaning: By yourself, with no help from anyone. ---
examples: She single-handedly raised four kids.
He won the game almost single-handedly.
You can't fix the economy single-handedly.
entries.contrast: single-handed is also used as the adverb with the same meaning (she sailed around the world single-handed); single-handedly is more common in American English.

entries.meaning: With all your attention on one goal. ---
examples: She worked single-mindedly toward her medical degree.
The company is single-mindedly focused on profit.
He pursued the record single-mindedly for ten years.

entries.meaning: One at a time or one by one; separately. ---
examples: Guests arrived singly or in pairs.
The stamps can be bought singly or in books of twenty.
These birds usually hunt singly.

entries.meaning: Extremely, to an unusual degree. ---
examples: The press conference was singularly unhelpful.
He was singularly unqualified for the job.
It was a singularly beautiful evening.
entries.modifies: adjectives, often negative or unfavorable ones

entries.meaning: By six times as much. ---
examples: The cost of the project increased sixfold.
Sales of electric bikes grew sixfold in five years.
The risk of injury rises sixfold without a helmet.
entries.modifies: verbs such as increase, grow, rise

entries.meaning: In a way that shows doubt. ---
examples: She raised an eyebrow skeptically.
Many scientists viewed the claim skeptically.
"You made this yourself?" he asked skeptically.
entries.contrast: British spelling is sceptically.

entries.meaning: Without many details; only in a rough or incomplete way. ---
examples: The accident was only sketchily reported in the local paper.
She described her plans sketchily, leaving out the important parts.
Early maps showed the coastline very sketchily.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (sketchily reported)
entries.contrast: Informal sketchy also means 'suspicious, unsafe' (a sketchy neighborhood); sketchily almost always means 'without detail'.

entries.meaning: With skill; very well. ---
examples: The pilot skillfully landed the damaged plane.
The story is skillfully told.
She handled the angry customers skillfully.
entries.contrast: British spelling is skilfully.

entries.meaning: With very little clothing, or with too little of something. ---
examples: The dancers were skimpily dressed.
A few skimpily clad tourists were shivering on the beach.
The report was skimpily researched.
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (skimpily dressed)

entries.meaning: Very high, or to a very high level. ---
examples: Rents in the city have shot sky-high.
The explosion blew the roof sky-high.
After the win, the team's confidence soared sky-high.
entries.modifies: verbs such as soar, shoot up, blow
entries.contrast: Before a noun it is an adjective: sky-high prices.

entries.meaning: Up toward the sky. ---
examples: The rocket rose skyward.
She pointed skyward at the eagle.
Gas prices are heading skyward again.

entries.meaning: Too closely, without any independent thought. ---
examples: The remake slavishly copies the original film.
Don't follow the recipe slavishly — taste as you go.
He slavishly does whatever his boss says.

entries.meaning: In a smooth, elegant and modern-looking way. ---
examples: The new phone is sleekly designed, with no buttons on the front.
The car's roof curves sleekly toward the back.
She wore her hair sleekly pulled back.
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (sleekly designed); also end

entries.meaning: In a tired way, as if almost asleep. ---
examples: "What time is it?" he asked sleepily.
She rubbed her eyes sleepily.
The cat stretched sleepily in the sun.

entries.meaning: In a smooth, polished way, sometimes too polished to seem sincere. ---
examples: The ad was slickly produced but said very little.
The campaign was slickly run from start to finish.
He answered the questions slickly, without really answering them.
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (slickly produced); also end

entries.meaning: Carelessly, without enough attention or effort. ---
examples: The report was sloppily written and full of errors.
He dresses sloppily even for important meetings.
The paint was applied sloppily around the windows.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (sloppily written)

entries.meaning: Slowly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Please speak more slowly.
She slowly opened the door.
The line was moving slowly.
The economy is slowly recovering.
Slowly but surely, the kids got used to their new school.

senses.head: At a low speed; not quickly
examples: Please speak more slowly.
She slowly opened the door.
The line was moving slowly.

senses.head: Gradually, little by little over time
examples: The economy is slowly recovering.
Slowly but surely, the kids got used to their new school.

entries.contrast: The comparative is more slowly or informal slower, never slowlier. Flat slow is informal and goes only after the verb (drive slow); before the verb use slowly (She slowly opened the door).

entries.meaning: Slowly and with little energy. ---
examples: The river moved sluggishly in the heat.
My old laptop runs sluggishly these days.
The stock market opened sluggishly on Monday.

entries.meaning: In a clever, secretive or playfully knowing way. ---
examples: She smiled slyly and said nothing.
He slyly slipped the cookie into his pocket.
The movie slyly pokes fun at Hollywood.

entries.meaning: Exactly or directly, often with force. ---
examples: The restaurant is smack in the middle of downtown.
He ran smack into a glass door.
Our vacation fell smack in the middle of hurricane season.
entries.position: before its word — before a preposition or adverb (smack in the middle)
entries.modifies: prepositional phrases and adverbs such as into, in the middle
entries.form: flat — the same form as the noun and verb smack
entries.contrast: Informal. smack-dab is a common American variant: smack-dab in the middle of town.

entries.meaning: In a small size or on a small scale. ---
examples: It's smart to start small and grow the business over time.
Don't think small — aim for the top.
Can you write a little smaller so it fits on the card?
entries.modifies: verbs such as start, think, write
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective small
entries.contrast: Mostly in fixed phrases: start small, think small, write small. small before a noun (a small car) is the adjective.

entries.meaning: Smartly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He was smartly dressed in a gray suit.
The lobby is smartly decorated in black and white.
The app is smartly designed and easy to use.
She smartly decided to wait until prices dropped.
The coach smartly used his time-outs at the end of the game.

senses.head: In a neat, stylish way
examples: He was smartly dressed in a gray suit.
The lobby is smartly decorated in black and white.

senses.head: Cleverly and sensibly
examples: The app is smartly designed and easy to use.
She smartly decided to wait until prices dropped.
The coach smartly used his time-outs at the end of the game.

entries.position: before its word — before a participle (smartly dressed); also end

entries.meaning: Smoothly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The move went more smoothly than we expected.
Everything is running smoothly at the new office.
We want the transition to go smoothly.
The car shifts gears smoothly.
The skater glided smoothly across the ice.

senses.head: Without problems or difficulties
examples: The move went more smoothly than we expected.
Everything is running smoothly at the new office.
We want the transition to go smoothly.

senses.head: With an even, steady movement
examples: The car shifts gears smoothly.
The skater glided smoothly across the ice.

entries.meaning: In a way that shows you are too pleased with yourself. ---
examples: "I told you so," she said smugly.
He smiled smugly when his team scored.
They sat back smugly, sure they had won the argument.

entries.meaning: In a secret, slightly dishonest way. ---
examples: He sneakily ate the last piece of cake.
The fee was sneakily added to the bill.
She glanced sneakily at her phone during the meeting.

entries.meaning: In an unkind, indirectly insulting way. ---
examples: "Nice haircut," he said snidely.
One critic snidely called the film a two-hour commercial.
She remarked snidely that some people never do any work.

entries.meaning: In a way that treats other people as inferior. ---
examples: The waiter looked at our shoes snobbishly.
She snobbishly refused to shop anywhere but the most expensive stores.
He talked snobbishly about "real" coffee.

entries.meaning: Snugly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The lid fits snugly on the jar.
Make sure the helmet fits snugly.
The baby was snugly wrapped in a blanket.
The cabin sits snugly in a valley.

senses.head: Closely and tightly, with no space left over
examples: The lid fits snugly on the jar.
Make sure the helmet fits snugly.

senses.head: Warmly and comfortably
examples: The baby was snugly wrapped in a blanket.
The cabin sits snugly in a valley.

entries.position: end — also before a participle (snugly wrapped)

entries.meaning: So far has 2 distinct senses.
examples: So far, so good.
We've had no problems so far.
The police have so far made two arrests.
I trust him only so far.
Money can only take you so far.

senses.head: Up to now; until this moment
examples: So far, so good.
We've had no problems so far.
The police have so far made two arrests.

senses.head: Only to a limited degree, usually with only
body: (до определённой степени, лишь до некоторой степени)
examples: I trust him only so far.
Money can only take you so far.

entries.русский: пока, до сих пор; до определённой степени
entries.position: front or end — mid with the present perfect (has so far refused)
entries.modifies: a whole clause; with only, verbs of trusting or going
entries.contrast: In the until now sense American English still prefers the present perfect: So far we've sold 200 tickets. Russian пока also means for now and bye, which so far never does.

entries.meaning: Used to show that a word is not meant exactly or literally. ---
examples: He's the black sheep of the family, so to speak.
We're all in the same boat, so to speak.
The new manager is, so to speak, still learning the ropes.
entries.type: viewpoint — flags a word used loosely or figuratively
entries.modifies: a word or phrase just used

entries.meaning: Not very well and not very badly. ---
examples: "How did the interview go?" "So-so."
Business has been going so-so this year.
The team played so-so in the first half.
entries.modifies: verbs such as go, do, play
entries.contrast: Informal. Before a noun it is an adjective: a so-so movie.

entries.meaning: Completely, used in soaking wet. ---
examples: I got caught in the rain and came home soaking wet.
The towels are still soaking wet.
By the end of the water fight, everyone was soaking wet.
entries.form: -ing form of soak, used like completely

entries.meaning: Soberly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We need to think soberly about the risks.
The president spoke soberly about the losses.
The mourners were soberly dressed in black.
The office is soberly furnished in gray and brown.

senses.head: In a serious, calm and sensible way
examples: We need to think soberly about the risks.
The president spoke soberly about the losses.

senses.head: In plain, dark colors, with no bright decoration
examples: The mourners were soberly dressed in black.
The office is soberly furnished in gray and brown.

entries.meaning: In terms of income, education and social class. ---
examples: The program helps students from socioeconomically disadvantaged families.
The neighborhood is racially and socioeconomically diverse.
Socioeconomically, the two groups were very similar.
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; also front
entries.modifies: adjectives and participles; a whole clause

entries.meaning: From the point of view of sociology, the study of society. ---
examples: Sociologically speaking, the suburbs changed American family life.
The rise of online dating is sociologically fascinating.
The study is sociologically important but hard to read.
entries.position: front — or before an adjective (sociologically interesting)

entries.meaning: Softly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She spoke softly so she wouldn't wake the baby.
Music played softly in the background.
Rain was falling softly on the roof.
He softly touched her arm.
Knock softly — Grandpa is sleeping.
The room was softly lit by candles.

senses.head: Quietly, not loudly
examples: She spoke softly so she wouldn't wake the baby.
Music played softly in the background.
Rain was falling softly on the roof.

senses.head: Gently, with little force
examples: He softly touched her arm.
Knock softly — Grandpa is sleeping.
The room was softly lit by candles.

entries.meaning: In a very serious and formal way. ---
examples: I solemnly swear to tell the truth.
The boy nodded solemnly.
The crowd stood solemnly for a moment of silence.

entries.meaning: In a caring way that shows concern for someone's comfort or health. ---
examples: "Are you warm enough?" the nurse asked solicitously.
He hovered solicitously around his pregnant wife.
The staff treated the older guests solicitously.

entries.meaning: Solidly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The old barn is solidly built.
The team played solidly all season.
The county has voted solidly Republican for decades.
It rained solidly for three days.
The staff is solidly behind the new plan.

senses.head: Firmly and strongly; reliably well
examples: The old barn is solidly built.
The team played solidly all season.

senses.head: Completely and consistently, with no break or exception
examples: The county has voted solidly Republican for decades.
It rained solidly for three days.
The staff is solidly behind the new plan.

entries.position: end — or before a participle or adjective (solidly built, solidly Democratic)

entries.meaning: Alone, without anyone else. ---
examples: She flew solo for the first time at sixteen.
He left the band in 2015 to go solo.
I like traveling solo.
entries.modifies: verbs such as fly, travel, go, perform
entries.contrast: Also a noun (a guitar solo) and an adjective (a solo album). Go solo means leave a band or group to work alone.

entries.meaning: In a sad, serious or dark way. ---
examples: The families waited somberly for news of the miners.
"There's nothing more we can do," the doctor said somberly.
The guests were somberly dressed in dark suits.
entries.contrast: British spelling is sombrely.

entries.meaning: Some has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The fire destroyed some 200 homes.
The village is some ten miles from the coast.
Some forty percent of voters stayed home.
I need to rest some before we keep going.
It's warmed up some since this morning.

senses.head: About, approximately, before a number
examples: The fire destroyed some 200 homes.
The village is some ten miles from the coast.
Some forty percent of voters stayed home.

senses.head: To some degree; a little (informal American)
examples: I need to rest some before we keep going.
It's warmed up some since this morning.

entries.position: before its word — before a number; end in the informal sense
entries.contrast: Before a noun some is a determiner (some water). As an adverb it means 'about' before a number. The end-position use (rest some) is informal American speech, not written English.

entries.meaning: In or to a place that is not named or known. ---
examples: Let's go someplace quiet to talk.
I left my keys someplace in the kitchen.
They moved someplace in Arizona.
entries.modifies: verbs; takes else and an adjective after it (someplace quiet)
entries.contrast: Informal American for somewhere. Like somewhere, it takes an adjective after it: someplace warm, not warm someplace.

entries.meaning: At a time that is not known or not stated, in the past or future. ---
examples: Let's have lunch sometime.
The house was built sometime in the 1920s.
I'll call you sometime next week.
entries.modifies: verbs; often followed by a time phrase (sometime next week)
entries.contrast: sometime (at some point) is not sometimes (occasionally), and neither is some time (a period of time): Call me sometime; I sometimes call her; It took some time.

entries.meaning: Before long; sooner or later, as you would expect. ---
examples: Don't worry, you'll find a job soon enough.
Soon enough, the kids were fast asleep.
He'll learn the truth soon enough.

entries.meaning: At some time in the future, and certainly. ---
examples: Sooner or later you'll have to tell her.
Everyone gets caught sooner or later.
He knew sooner or later the money would run out.

entries.meaning: In a calm way that makes someone feel less upset or in less pain. ---
examples: "It's okay, you're safe now," she said soothingly.
He talked soothingly to the frightened horse.
The music was soothingly quiet.

entries.meaning: Completely, used in sopping wet. ---
examples: My socks were sopping wet after the walk through the field.
The dog came in from the rain sopping wet.
Don't leave that sopping wet towel on the bed.
entries.form: -ing form of sop, used like completely

entries.meaning: Very much; badly. ---
examples: The town is sorely in need of a new hospital.
Your help was sorely missed.
I was sorely tempted to quit on the spot.
entries.position: mid — before a participle or verb (sorely needed)
entries.modifies: participles and verbs such as needed, missed, tempted, disappointed

entries.meaning: Somewhat; in a way; to some degree. ---
examples: I sort of like him.
The room was sort of dark and cold.
It sort of makes sense, I guess.
entries.position: before its word — an adjective or verb
entries.modifies: adjectives, verbs, whole answers (“Did you like it?” “Sort of.”)
entries.contrast: Kind of means the same. A sort of + noun is a noun phrase meaning a type of (a sort of soup), not the adverb. Informal; often written sorta in dialogue.

entries.meaning: With deep feeling, often sad feeling. ---
examples: She sang the old hymn soulfully.
The dog gazed soulfully at my sandwich.
A saxophone played soulfully on the street corner.

entries.meaning: Without making any sound. ---
examples: The cat moved soundlessly across the floor.
Her lips moved soundlessly as she read.
The door swung soundlessly open.

entries.meaning: Soundly has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The kids were sleeping soundly when we got home.
I slept soundly for the first time in weeks.
The incumbent was soundly defeated in the election.
We got beaten soundly in the final.
The argument is soundly based on the evidence.
The money was soundly invested.

senses.head: Deeply, of sleep
examples: The kids were sleeping soundly when we got home.
I slept soundly for the first time in weeks.

senses.head: Completely and clearly, of a defeat
examples: The incumbent was soundly defeated in the election.
We got beaten soundly in the final.

senses.head: Sensibly and reliably, on a good basis
examples: The argument is soundly based on the evidence.
The money was soundly invested.

entries.position: end — or before a participle (soundly based)

entries.meaning: In an unfriendly, bad-tempered or disappointed way. ---
examples: "Great, another meeting," he said sourly.
She looked sourly at the pile of dishes.
Fans reacted sourly to the trade.

entries.meaning: Toward or in the south. ---
examples: Many birds fly south for the winter.
We drove south on I-95.
The airport is about twenty miles south of the city.
entries.modifies: verbs of motion, and be, live, lie
entries.contrast: As an adverb it takes no preposition: drive south, fly south, not drive to south. Use to the south or in the south when it is a noun. down south is common in American speech, often meaning the Southern states: My grandparents live down south.

entries.meaning: Toward or in the southeast. ---
examples: The hurricane is moving southeast, away from the coast.
The town is fifteen miles southeast of Atlanta.
Turn southeast at the next intersection.
entries.modifies: verbs of motion, and be, live, lie
entries.form: south + east, written as one word in American English

entries.meaning: Toward or in the southwest. ---
examples: We drove southwest toward the desert.
The ranch lies forty miles southwest of Tucson.
The trail heads southwest from the parking lot.
entries.modifies: verbs of motion, and be, live, lie
entries.form: south + west, written as one word in American English

entries.meaning: In small amounts; not much or not often. ---
examples: Use the hot sauce sparingly — it's really strong.
The coach uses his young players sparingly.
Water the plant sparingly in winter.
entries.modifies: verbs such as use, eat, apply

entries.meaning: With only a few people or things spread over an area. ---
examples: Wyoming is the most sparsely populated state.
The apartment was sparsely furnished.
The early show was sparsely attended.
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (sparsely populated)
entries.modifies: participles such as populated, furnished, attended

entries.meaning: Spasmodically has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He worked on the book only spasmodically.
Fighting continued spasmodically through the night.
His leg twitched spasmodically.
The fish flapped spasmodically on the deck.

senses.head: Now and then, not regularly or continuously
examples: He worked on the book only spasmodically.
Fighting continued spasmodically through the night.

senses.head: With sudden movements of the muscles that you cannot control
examples: His leg twitched spasmodically.
The fish flapped spasmodically on the deck.

entries.meaning: In terms of space, size or position. ---
examples: Some people are spatially gifted and can read maps easily.
The data were mapped spatially across the country.
The two buildings are spatially close but feel very different.

entries.meaning: Specially has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The kitchen was specially designed for a wheelchair user.
I made this cake specially for you.
The trucks are specially equipped for snow.
It's a specially hard time of year for us.
He's not specially interested in sports.

senses.head: For a particular purpose or person
examples: The kitchen was specially designed for a wheelchair user.
I made this cake specially for you.
The trucks are specially equipped for snow.

senses.head: Particularly; more than usual (informal)
examples: It's a specially hard time of year for us.
He's not specially interested in sports.

entries.position: before its word — before a participle (specially designed); also end
entries.contrast: specially mainly means 'for a particular purpose' (specially made). For 'above all, particularly' the standard word is especially (I love fruit, especially apples); specially in that sense is informal speech.

entries.meaning: In a very impressive or dramatic way; to a very great degree. ---
examples: The plan failed spectacularly.
The canyon is spectacularly beautiful at sunset.
Her first business succeeded spectacularly.
entries.position: end — or before an adjective (spectacularly beautiful)

entries.meaning: As a guess, without firm evidence. ---
examples: Some writers have speculatively linked the two events.
The report speculatively puts the final cost at $2 billion.
He talked speculatively about running for office someday.

entries.meaning: Quickly; without delay. ---
examples: The problem was speedily resolved.
The judge wants the case handled speedily.
Volunteers worked speedily to fill the sandbags.

entries.meaning: In a way that concerns the soul, religion, or inner life. ---
examples: After the retreat, she felt spiritually renewed.
Many people are spiritually hungry but never go to church.
Spiritually, the trip changed his life.
entries.position: before its word — before adjectives and participles (spiritually renewed); also front

entries.meaning: With a wish to hurt or annoy someone. ---
examples: She spitefully deleted all his photos.
'Good luck with that,' he said spitefully.
The neighbor spitefully parked across our driveway.
entries.position: end — or mid, before the verb

entries.meaning: Very well; in an impressive way. ---
examples: The kids behaved splendidly at the wedding.
Everything went splendidly.
The hall was splendidly decorated for the holidays.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (splendidly decorated)

entries.meaning: Spontaneously has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The crowd spontaneously broke into applause.
We decided spontaneously to drive to the beach.
The pile of oily rags spontaneously caught fire.
In most cases the pain goes away spontaneously.

senses.head: Without planning, on a sudden impulse
examples: The crowd spontaneously broke into applause.
We decided spontaneously to drive to the beach.

senses.head: By itself, without an outside cause
examples: The pile of oily rags spontaneously caught fire.
In most cases the pain goes away spontaneously.

entries.meaning: In a strange, slightly frightening way. ---
examples: Her prediction turned out to be spookily accurate.
The two sisters look spookily alike.
The wind howled spookily through the empty house.
entries.position: before its word — spookily accurate; end with verbs

entries.meaning: Perfectly, with no dirt at all. ---
examples: The kitchen was spotlessly clean.
He keeps his car spotlessly clean.
The hotel rooms were spotlessly maintained.
entries.position: before its word — almost always spotlessly clean

entries.meaning: Directly and exactly. ---
examples: She looked me square in the eye and said no.
The ball hit him square in the face.
The dart landed square in the center of the board.
entries.position: end — right before in or on (square in the eye)
entries.modifies: verbs of hitting, landing, and looking
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective square
entries.contrast: Informal; careful writing uses squarely. Fair and square is a fixed phrase meaning 'honestly, by the rules': We won fair and square.

entries.meaning: Squarely has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The blame lies squarely with the management.
The ball hit him squarely on the head.
The new law is aimed squarely at small businesses.
It's time we faced the problem squarely.
The senator refused to answer the question squarely.

senses.head: Directly, exactly, and fully
examples: The blame lies squarely with the management.
The ball hit him squarely on the head.
The new law is aimed squarely at small businesses.

senses.head: Openly and honestly, without avoiding something
examples: It's time we faced the problem squarely.
The senator refused to answer the question squarely.

entries.position: end — or before a phrase with on, at, with (squarely on the table)

entries.meaning: To an amazing, almost unbelievable degree. ---
examples: The house was staggeringly expensive.
It's a staggeringly beautiful place.
The cost of the war was staggeringly high.

entries.meaning: Completely, in a couple of fixed phrases. ---
examples: The toddler ran out of the bathroom stark naked.
You'd have to be stark raving mad to swim out there in January.
The kids were running around the backyard stark naked.
entries.position: before its word — only in stark naked and stark raving mad
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective stark
entries.contrast: Only in these two fixed phrases. Elsewhere stark is an adjective (a stark contrast, stark reality), and its adverb is starkly.

entries.meaning: In a sharp, clear, often harsh way. ---
examples: The two candidates have starkly different views on taxes.
The report starkly warns of a coming water shortage.
Her bright dress stood out starkly against the gray walls.
entries.position: before its word — starkly different; end with verbs

entries.meaning: To a surprising, even shocking, degree. ---
examples: She has startlingly blue eyes.
The results were startlingly similar.
Prices rose startlingly fast last year.

entries.meaning: Firmly and loyally, without changing your position. ---
examples: Her family is staunchly conservative.
He staunchly defended his decision.
The union staunchly opposes the plan.
entries.position: mid — or before its word (staunchly conservative)
entries.modifies: verbs of supporting and opposing; adjectives of political views

entries.meaning: Firmly, without giving in or changing. ---
examples: She steadfastly refused to name her sources.
He remained steadfastly loyal to his friends.
The company has steadfastly denied any wrongdoing.
entries.modifies: verbs of refusing and denying; adjectives like loyal

entries.meaning: Steadily has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Prices have risen steadily over the past year.
The snow fell steadily all night.
Her health is steadily improving.
He looked at her steadily and waited.
She spoke steadily despite her nerves.

senses.head: Gradually and continuously, without stopping
examples: Prices have risen steadily over the past year.
The snow fell steadily all night.
Her health is steadily improving.

senses.head: Firmly and calmly, without shaking or looking away
examples: He looked at her steadily and waited.
She spoke steadily despite her nerves.

entries.meaning: Quietly and secretly, so as not to be noticed. ---
examples: The cat crept stealthily toward the bird.
He stealthily slipped out the back door.
They moved stealthily through the dark hallway.
entries.position: end — or mid, before the verb

entries.meaning: Extremely; mostly in steaming hot. ---
examples: Be careful, the soup is steaming hot.
The waiter set down two steaming hot plates of pasta.
Dad was steaming mad when he saw the dent in the car.
entries.position: before its word — hot, and informally mad
entries.form: the -ing form of steam, used as a degree word

entries.meaning: At a sharp angle; sharply, of a rise or fall. ---
examples: The road climbs steeply into the hills.
Home prices fell steeply after the crash.
The path drops steeply down to the river.

entries.meaning: Gradually, one stage at a time. ---
examples: The video explains the process step by step.
We rebuilt the business step by step.
Take it step by step and don't rush.
entries.contrast: Hyphenated before a noun it is an adjective: step-by-step instructions.

entries.meaning: In a way that matches a fixed, oversimplified idea of a group. ---
examples: Pink was once seen as a stereotypically feminine color.
He's a stereotypically grumpy New York cab driver.
In the movie, the villain is stereotypically portrayed as a foreigner.
entries.position: before its word — before adjectives (stereotypically feminine); also end

entries.meaning: In a serious, strict, disapproving way. ---
examples: 'Sit down,' the teacher said sternly.
The judge sternly warned the jury not to discuss the case.
She looked at him sternly over her glasses.
entries.position: end — or mid, before the verb

entries.meaning: Extremely, after a few participles. ---
examples: I was bored stiff at that meeting.
The kids were scared stiff of the dog.
By the time we got home, we were frozen stiff.
entries.русский: до смерти, ужасно (bored stiff — до смерти скучно)
entries.position: after its word — after bored, scared, frozen, worried
entries.form: flat — the same form as the adjective stiff
entries.contrast: Informal and only after these few words. Elsewhere stiff is an adjective (a stiff neck), and the manner adverb is stiffly.

entries.meaning: Stiffly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He got up stiffly after the long flight.
The old man walked stiffly to the door.
'I have nothing to say,' she replied stiffly.
They shook hands stiffly and sat down.

senses.head: In a rigid way, without bending easily
examples: He got up stiffly after the long flight.
The old man walked stiffly to the door.

senses.head: In a cold, formal, unfriendly way
examples: 'I have nothing to say,' she replied stiffly.
They shook hands stiffly and sat down.

entries.meaning: Completely without moving. ---
examples: The deer stood stock-still in the headlights.
We froze stock-still when we heard the noise.
The children sat stock-still as the magician raised his hands.

entries.meaning: Calmly and without complaining, in spite of pain or trouble. ---
examples: She stoically endured months of treatment.
He listened stoically as the verdict was read.
The fans waited stoically in the freezing rain.

entries.meaning: Calmly and without showing any feeling. ---
examples: He stared stolidly ahead, saying nothing.
The guard stood stolidly at the gate.
She chewed her food stolidly while the others argued.

entries.meaning: Coldly, without any friendly feeling. ---
examples: She stared at him stonily and said nothing.
He listened stonily to their apologies.
The audience sat stonily through his jokes.

entries.meaning: Firmly and bravely, of defending or denying something. ---
examples: He stoutly denied taking the money.
Local residents stoutly opposed the new highway.
She stoutly defended her son's behavior.
entries.modifies: verbs of defending, denying, and opposing

entries.meaning: Immediately. ---
examples: I knew straightaway that something was wrong.
She called the police straightaway.
Can you start straightaway?
entries.contrast: More common in British English; Americans usually say right away, though straightaway is still met in American reading. Also written straight away.

entries.meaning: In a direct, honest, or uncomplicated way. ---
examples: She answered the question straightforwardly.
The instructions are written straightforwardly, so anyone can follow them.
He told us straightforwardly that the project had failed.

entries.meaning: Strangely has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He's been acting strangely all week.
The house was strangely quiet.
She looked at me strangely.
Strangely enough, nobody noticed.
Strangely, I wasn't nervous at all.

senses.head: In an unusual or odd way
examples: He's been acting strangely all week.
The house was strangely quiet.
She looked at me strangely.

senses.head: Surprisingly; a comment on a fact, often in strangely enough
examples: Strangely enough, nobody noticed.
Strangely, I wasn't nervous at all.

entries.position: end — or before its word (strangely quiet); front as a comment

entries.meaning: In a way that is planned to achieve a goal or gain an advantage. ---
examples: Cameras were strategically placed around the building.
The town is strategically important.
We need to think strategically about the next five years.
entries.position: before its word — before adjectives and participles (strategically placed); also end

entries.meaning: With great effort or force, especially in objecting or denying. ---
examples: The senator strenuously denied the charges.
Parents strenuously objected to the new schedule.
Avoid exercising strenuously for a week after surgery.
entries.modifies: verbs of objecting and denying; verbs of effort

entries.meaning: Strictly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Smoking is strictly forbidden inside the building.
The rules are strictly enforced.
Strictly speaking, a tomato is a fruit.
This is strictly a business meeting.
The information is strictly for your eyes.

senses.head: Firmly, so that rules must be obeyed; also exactly, in strictly speaking
examples: Smoking is strictly forbidden inside the building.
The rules are strictly enforced.
Strictly speaking, a tomato is a fruit.

senses.head: Only; for no other purpose
examples: This is strictly a business meeting.
The information is strictly for your eyes.

entries.position: before its word — before participles (strictly forbidden); front in strictly speaking

entries.meaning: If you use words in their exact, correct sense. ---
examples: Strictly speaking, a tomato is a fruit.
Strictly speaking, we're not allowed to park here.
It's not, strictly speaking, a new idea.
entries.type: viewpoint — using a word in its exact meaning

entries.meaning: In a loud, harsh, forceful way, especially in giving opinions. ---
examples: She stridently criticized the new law.
He argued stridently for lower taxes.
The group has become stridently opposed to any compromise.
entries.position: end — or mid, before the verb
entries.modifies: verbs of speaking and arguing; adjectives of opinion

entries.meaning: In a way that is very noticeable or impressive. ---
examples: She's a strikingly beautiful woman.
The two paintings are strikingly similar.
Crime rates dropped strikingly fast in the 1990s.

entries.meaning: Very strictly, with tough rules or standards. ---
examples: New drugs are stringently tested before approval.
The rules are applied stringently to all applicants.
Air quality is stringently regulated in California.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (stringently tested)
entries.modifies: verbs and participles of testing and controlling

entries.meaning: In a determined way that refuses to change or give up. ---
examples: He stubbornly refused to ask for directions.
Unemployment remains stubbornly high.
She held on stubbornly to her old ideas.
entries.position: mid or end — also before its word (stubbornly high)

entries.meaning: Carefully and deliberately. ---
examples: She studiously avoided looking at him.
The report studiously ignores the real problem.
He studiously took notes during every lecture.
entries.contrast: Usually not about studying: studiously avoided means 'carefully, on purpose avoided'.

entries.meaning: Extremely, in a way that amazes you. ---
examples: The view from the top is stunningly beautiful.
The plan was stunningly simple.
The team played stunningly well.

entries.meaning: To an amazing degree. ---
examples: The owner of the team is stupendously rich.
The project turned out to be stupendously expensive.
The band played stupendously well that night.

entries.meaning: Stupidly has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She stared stupidly at the screen, unable to think.
He was grinning stupidly at his phone.
Stupidly, I left my wallet in the car.
I stupidly forgot to save the file.

senses.head: In a foolish or dazed way
examples: She stared stupidly at the screen, unable to think.
He was grinning stupidly at his phone.

senses.head: Used to say that something you did was foolish
examples: Stupidly, I left my wallet in the car.
I stupidly forgot to save the file.

entries.position: end — or front and mid as a comment

entries.meaning: Strongly and solidly. ---
examples: The table is sturdily built.
He's a sturdily built man in his fifties.
The shelves are sturdily made of oak.
entries.position: before its word — mostly in sturdily built

entries.meaning: In a fashionable, attractive way. ---
examples: She's always stylishly dressed.
The apartment is stylishly decorated.
The film is stylishly shot but boring.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (stylishly dressed)

entries.meaning: In terms of style. ---
examples: Stylistically, the two books are very different.
The songs are stylistically similar.
The essay is stylistically weak but full of good ideas.
entries.position: front or end — also before adjectives (stylistically similar)

entries.meaning: Without being aware of it. ---
examples: Maybe you subconsciously wanted to fail.
We subconsciously copy the body language of people we like.
He was subconsciously looking for an excuse to leave.

entries.meaning: Based on personal feelings or opinions, not facts. ---
examples: Beauty is judged subjectively.
Subjectively, the pain felt much worse than it was.
The essays are graded somewhat subjectively.
entries.position: end — or front as a viewpoint

entries.meaning: Wonderfully; also completely, as in sublimely unaware. ---
examples: The music was sublimely beautiful.
He seemed sublimely unaware of the trouble he'd caused.
She played the second movement sublimely.
entries.position: before its word — sublimely beautiful, sublimely unaware; end with verbs

entries.meaning: In a way that obeys others without arguing. ---
examples: The dog rolled over submissively.
She lowered her eyes submissively.
He nodded submissively and did as he was told.

entries.meaning: Substantially has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Costs have increased substantially this year.
The new model is substantially cheaper.
Our plans changed substantially after the merger.
The two versions are substantially the same.
The report is substantially correct.

senses.head: By a large amount; considerably
examples: Costs have increased substantially this year.
The new model is substantially cheaper.
Our plans changed substantially after the merger.

senses.head: In the main points; essentially
examples: The two versions are substantially the same.
The report is substantially correct.

entries.position: mid or end — also before its word (substantially cheaper)

entries.meaning: In a slight, clever, or hard-to-notice way. ---
examples: The two versions are subtly different.
She subtly changed the subject.
The room was subtly lit with candles.
entries.position: mid or end — also before adjectives (subtly different)
entries.form: -ly from subtle: the -le becomes -ly, and the b stays silent

entries.meaning: In a way that achieves the result you wanted. ---
examples: The surgery was successfully completed.
She successfully ran her own business for twenty years.
The rocket launched successfully this morning.

entries.meaning: One after another, in order. ---
examples: The tests become successively harder.
Each generation has been successively taller than the last.
The company was successively owned by three different families.
entries.position: before its word — before comparatives (successively harder); also mid
entries.contrast: Not successfully: successively means 'one after another' (последовательно), successfully means 'with success' (успешно).

entries.meaning: Clearly and in very few words. ---
examples: She summed up the problem succinctly.
Please answer each question succinctly.
As one critic put it succinctly, 'Too long.'

entries.meaning: To so great a degree, before an adjective and its noun. ---
examples: It was such a beautiful day that we stayed outside.
They're such nice people.
I've never eaten such good pizza.
entries.position: before its word — before (a/an +) adjective + noun
entries.modifies: an adjective together with its noun
entries.contrast: Such goes before a noun phrase, so before an adjective alone: such a nice day, but the day was so nice. The article comes after it: such a, never a such. As a determiner (such people, no such thing) it is not an adverb.

entries.meaning: Enough for a purpose. ---
examples: The patient has sufficiently recovered to go home.
The room wasn't sufficiently large for the party.
Make sure the chicken is sufficiently cooked.

entries.meaning: In a way that hints at something, especially something sexual. ---
examples: He winked at her suggestively.
She raised her eyebrows suggestively.
The ad was criticized for how suggestively the models were posed.

entries.meaning: In the right way or to the right degree for the situation. ---
examples: Make sure you're suitably dressed for the interview.
Everyone was suitably impressed by the view.
The children were suitably rewarded for their hard work.
entries.position: before its word — before adjectives and participles (suitably dressed)

entries.meaning: In a silent, bad-tempered way, because you are annoyed. ---
examples: 'I don't want to go,' he said sulkily.
She sat sulkily in the corner all evening.
The teenager shuffled sulkily up to his room.

entries.meaning: In a gloomy, unfriendly way. ---
examples: He stared sullenly out the window.
The prisoners listened sullenly to the new rules.
She answered sullenly and went back to her phone.

entries.meaning: With the highest honors, of graduating from a college. ---
examples: She graduated summa cum laude from Yale.
Only five students finished summa cum laude this year.
He graduated magna cum laude, not summa cum laude.
entries.type: manner — with the highest academic honors
entries.contrast: American colleges use three levels: cum laude (with honors), magna cum laude (with high honors) and summa cum laude (with highest honors). It is not the same as a Russian красный диплом, which has one level.

entries.meaning: Immediately and without the usual discussion or legal process. ---
examples: He was summarily fired after the incident.
The rebels summarily executed their prisoners.
The judge summarily dismissed the case.
entries.position: before its word — before participles (summarily fired); also mid
entries.modifies: verbs of firing, dismissing, and punishing
entries.form: -ly from summary in its adjective sense 'quick and without formalities'
entries.contrast: Not 'in summary'. To mean 'to sum up', say in summary or in short.

entries.meaning: In a rich, expensive, impressive way. ---
examples: The hotel lobby is sumptuously decorated.
We dined sumptuously on lobster and champagne.
The book is sumptuously illustrated.
entries.position: before its word — before participles (sumptuously decorated); also end

entries.meaning: Extremely well. ---
examples: The team played superbly in the second half.
The hotel is superbly located near the beach.
She sang superbly.
entries.position: end — or before a participle (superbly located)

entries.meaning: Superficially has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The doctor only examined him superficially.
The book deals with the topic superficially.
The two cases are superficially similar.
Superficially, everything seemed fine.

senses.head: Only on the surface; without looking deeply
examples: The doctor only examined him superficially.
The book deals with the topic superficially.

senses.head: In appearance, but not in reality
examples: The two cases are superficially similar.
Superficially, everything seemed fine.

entries.position: end — or before adjectives (superficially similar); front as a viewpoint

entries.meaning: In a way that seems beyond the laws of nature; unbelievably. ---
examples: He seemed supernaturally strong for a man his size.
In the story, the old house is supernaturally protected.
She has an almost supernaturally good memory for faces.
entries.position: before its word — supernaturally strong; also end

entries.meaning: Because of a belief in luck or magic. ---
examples: He superstitiously wears the same socks to every game.
She knocked on wood superstitiously.
Many hotels superstitiously skip the thirteenth floor.

entries.meaning: Extremely; to the highest degree. ---
examples: She was supremely confident before the race.
It was a supremely important moment in his career.
The chef is supremely talented.

entries.meaning: As expected or predicted; and in fact. ---
examples: I said it would rain, and sure enough, it poured.
Sure enough, the store was closed when we got there.
I checked the drawer, and there it was, sure enough.
entries.position: front — with a comma, or end

entries.meaning: Surgically has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The tumor was surgically removed.
The broken bone had to be surgically repaired.
The editor surgically cut three scenes without hurting the story.
The new rule surgically closes a single tax loophole.

senses.head: By means of a medical operation
examples: The tumor was surgically removed.
The broken bone had to be surgically repaired.

senses.head: With great precision, touching only the intended target
examples: The editor surgically cut three scenes without hurting the story.
The new rule surgically closes a single tax loophole.

entries.position: before its word — before participles (surgically removed); also end

entries.meaning: Secretly, so that others do not notice. ---
examples: He surreptitiously checked his phone under the table.
She glanced surreptitiously at her watch.
The meeting was surreptitiously recorded.

entries.meaning: Suspiciously has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The guard eyed us suspiciously.
'Why do you ask?' she said suspiciously.
The kids are suspiciously quiet.
A man was acting suspiciously outside the bank.

senses.head: Without trusting someone; with suspicion
examples: The guard eyed us suspiciously.
'Why do you ask?' she said suspiciously.

senses.head: In a way that makes people suspect something is wrong
examples: The kids are suspiciously quiet.
A man was acting suspiciously outside the bank.

entries.position: end — or before its word (suspiciously quiet)

entries.meaning: In a pleasant, kind, or gentle way. ---
examples: She smiled sweetly at the waiter.
The baby was sleeping sweetly in her crib.
The choir sang sweetly.

entries.meaning: Quickly and without delay. ---
examples: The police acted swiftly to calm the crowd.
The river flows swiftly after heavy rain.
Prices rose swiftly after the announcement.

entries.meaning: Very smoothly, without any problems. ---
examples: The party went swimmingly.
So far, everything is going swimmingly.
The two dogs got along swimmingly.
entries.русский: как по маслу, без сучка без задоринки
entries.contrast: Informal and a little old-fashioned. It has nothing to do with swimming.

entries.meaning: As a symbol, to show a meaning or idea. ---
examples: She symbolically handed him the keys to the office.
The ceremony was held symbolically on the Fourth of July.
Symbolically, the new bridge joins two divided communities.
entries.position: mid or end — or front as a viewpoint

entries.meaning: With both sides or halves exactly alike. ---
examples: The windows are arranged symmetrically on both sides of the door.
Plant the trees symmetrically along the path.
The garden was laid out symmetrically.

entries.meaning: Sympathetically has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She listened sympathetically to his story.
The nurse smiled at me sympathetically.
The film portrays the rebels sympathetically.
The board looked sympathetically on her proposal.

senses.head: With kindness and understanding for someone's problems
examples: She listened sympathetically to his story.
The nurse smiled at me sympathetically.

senses.head: In a favorable way; with approval
examples: The film portrays the rebels sympathetically.
The board looked sympathetically on her proposal.

entries.contrast: False friend: it is about sympathy (сочувствие), not about being симпатичный — that is nice or good-looking.

entries.meaning: With the same meaning. ---
examples: The two terms are often used synonymously.
In this article, 'weather' and 'climate' are not used synonymously.
Many people use 'Holland' and 'the Netherlands' synonymously.

entries.meaning: By a chemical process, not naturally. ---
examples: The vitamin can be produced synthetically.
Synthetically made diamonds are much cheaper.
The fabric is synthetically dyed.
entries.position: before its word — before participles (synthetically produced); also end

entries.meaning: Using an organized method, step by step.
examples: The police systematically searched every house on the street.
Women were systematically excluded from the club.
We need to go through the data systematically.
